27 P and Q are fixed points at the end of a string. A transverse stationary wave of constant
maximum amplitude is formed on the string.
x
x
P
R
T
S
Q
P, R and Q are the only points on the string where nodes are formed. S and T are two points on
the string at a distance x from R.
What is the relationship between points S and T?
A
the same amplitude and in phase
B
different amplitudes and in phase
C
the same amplitude and a phase difference of 180°
D
different amplitudes and a phase difference of 180°

hints: Notice P, R and Q are the only nodes, so PR and RQ are two separate loops with R as a node between S and T.
Recall that in a stationary wave amplitude depends on distance from a node, so compare distance $x$ of S from R with distance $x$ of T from R.
Recall that all points in one loop are in phase but points in adjacent loops on opposite sides of a node move in opposite directions.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern from the diagram: nodes at P, R and Q mean there are two loops, one from P to R and one from R to Q, with R a node in the middle.
Locate S and T: S is distance $x$ to the left of R in the left loop, T is distance $x$ to the right of R in the right loop.

Use the amplitude rule for a stationary wave of constant maximum amplitude: amplitude is zero at a node and maximum at an antinode, and depends only on position within the loop. Equal distances from the node R give equal amplitudes, so S and T have the same amplitude.
Use the phase rule for a stationary wave: all points between two adjacent nodes vibrate in phase, but points separated by a node in adjacent loops vibrate in antiphase.
Since S and T are separated by node R and lie in different loops, when S moves up T moves down, which is a phase difference of $180^\circ$.
Same amplitude plus $180^\circ$ phase difference. This is option C.

A.explanation: Amplitude is the same because S and T are equally far from node R, but they cannot be in phase because they lie in different loops separated by a node.

B.explanation: S and T are in phase only if they are in the same loop, but S is in loop PR and T is in loop RQ so they vibrate in antiphase.

C.explanation: Equal distance $x$ from the node R gives equal vibration amplitude, and adjacent loops on opposite sides of a node vibrate with phase difference $180^\circ$.

D.explanation: The $180^\circ$ phase difference is correct for adjacent loops, but the amplitudes are the same because both points are distance $x$ from R with constant maximum amplitude.
